source: Nick Marchetti's prompt workbook, Participant prompt column

items.title: Level 1: ask Work IQ a one-line question
items.prompt: What issues are starting to build across my work that I should step into before they escalate?
items.feature: Work IQ: Copilot reads across your email, meetings, chats and files and cites its sources.
items.participant_tip: Leave the model on Auto. Run B1 to B4 in the same conversation.

items.title: Level 2: ask for specifics and a format
items.prompt: Which three issues are most likely to need a decision from my leadership team in the next month? For each one, tell me who is involved, where views differ, and what's at stake. Put it in a table.
items.feature: Better prompts: say what you want back, the detail and the format. Model choice.
items.participant_tip: Before sending, open the model picker and choose a Claude model to see a different writing style.

items.title: Level 3: add a file with / (Context IQ)
items.prompt: I'm preparing my leadership team for the next phase of integration with Coca-Cola HBC. Read /Coca-Cola HBC 2026 Half Year Results Presentation and compare Coca-Cola HBC's stated priorities with what my team has been discussing in my emails, meetings and chats over the last month. Show where we're aligned and where the gaps are in a table with sources, then give me three questions to raise with my leadership team. Write it for senior executives who have five minutes to read it.
items.feature: Context IQ: type / to insert a file, meeting, email or person, combined with Work IQ.
items.participant_tip: Download the Coca-Cola HBC 2026 Half Year Results Presentation first, save it to OneDrive and insert it with /, or attach it with +. Choose a reasoning model from the model picker before sending.

items.title: Level 4: turn it into a Page and draft the email
items.prompt: Turn this into a Page I can share with my leadership team. Then draft an email to [colleagues] with the three questions and a link to the Page, asking for their input before [meeting or date].
items.feature: Copilot Pages and an Outlook email drafted inside Chat.
items.participant_tip: If no Page appears, select Edit in Pages under the answer. Review the email draft before you send it.

items.title: Executive signal scan
items.prompt: Provide a concise executive scan of today's top priorities, critical decisions, and upcoming engagements from emails, Teams conversations, and calendar. Include: a brief of upcoming meetings with time and participants, high-priority emails requiring attention, mentions of my name in Teams chats or other communications, and any items that could materially affect the strategic initiative I am currently leading. Separate the output into: 1) What needs my attention today 2) What has strategic impact 3) What I can delegate or ignore. Present it in a dashboard format with columns: Category, Item, Priority, Time Sensitivity, Strategic Relevance, and Source.
items.feature: Work IQ across email, Teams and calendar in one daily briefing.

items.title: Save it and schedule it
items.prompt: Save your executive scan prompt (C1) to your saved prompts, then schedule it to run every weekday morning.
items.feature: Saved prompts and scheduled prompts: the briefing arrives every morning without asking.
items.participant_tip: This is an instruction, not a prompt. Show it as a step, with no copy button.

items.title: Executive Chief of Staff custom instructions
items.prompt:
Act as a senior executive advisor. Optimise responses for clarity, strategic relevance, and decision-making speed. Start with a concise executive summary, followed by key insights and clear recommendations. Focus on business impact, risks, trade-offs, and second-order effects. Challenge assumptions where appropriate and highlight what is uncertain. Avoid unnecessary technical detail unless explicitly requested. Use structured bullet points and plain business language.
- If I prefix a message with *1m, respond with a response readable in under 1 minute.
- If I prefix a message with *5m, respond with a response readable in under 5 minutes.
- If I prefix a message with *dd, provide structured detail after a summary.
- If I prefix a message with *pf, rewrite it to be polite, friendly, and collaborative. Soften direct language, add courtesy where appropriate, and maintain professionalism. Do not change the core intent or weaken accountability.
- If I prefix a message with *wm, rewrite the message to sound approachable, appreciative, and relationship-oriented. Acknowledge effort or context where appropriate. Avoid sounding formal or bureaucratic.
- If I prefix a message with *dp, rewrite the message to be tactful, non-confrontational, and carefully worded. Preserve intent while minimising friction or defensiveness.
- If I prefix *e, extract information from the image.
items.feature: Custom instructions (how Copilot writes for you) and prompt shortcuts.
items.participant_tip: Paste into Settings > Personalization > Custom instructions and save.

items.title: Test a shortcut
items.prompt: *1m What should I focus on this week?
items.feature: Shortcuts defined in your custom instructions.

items.title: Create personalized Copilot instructions
items.prompt:
I am [your role] at CCBA.

Review my sent emails, documents, meetings, and other work context to understand how I work.

Identify:
- My role and core responsibilities
- My biggest priorities and recurring areas of focus
- How I prefer information to be presented
- My communication and writing style
- The level of detail I typically use
- How I make decisions and what information I tend to care about
- People, teams, and topics I frequently work with

Turn what you learn into clear, concise Custom Instructions for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Write the instructions so Copilot knows how to work with me, how to communicate with me, and how to make its responses more useful to me.

Separate the output into:
- About me and my work
- How I want Copilot to respond
- My writing and communication style
- My default preferences

Make the final instructions ready for me to copy and paste into Custom Instructions.
items.feature: Work IQ writes custom instructions from your own work.

items.title: Compare and prioritize growth options
items.prompt:
Research how CCBA could strengthen customer-led, profitable growth in [market] over the next 12 to 24 months. Compare opportunities across affordable pack-price architecture, targeted channel and promotion choices, and improved product availability through distributor and outlet execution. Use current, credible sources and relevant examples from comparable African beverage and consumer-goods markets. Evaluate the potential customer impact, growth opportunity, profitability, risks and execution considerations of each approach. Clearly distinguish facts from assumptions and identify where internal CCBA data would be needed to validate your findings.

End with:
- The opportunity leadership should prioritize and why
- What CCBA should test first
- What internal data is needed to validate the recommendation
- What evidence could change the recommendation
- Five questions leadership should ask before making a decision
items.feature: Researcher agent.
items.note_for_jeff: Your Exercise 7 prompt 1, unchanged. Move Exercise 7 up to sit after Prompt Coach (we launch Researcher at that point and return to it later).

items.title: Assess demand and profitability forces
items.prompt:
Research the biggest forces that will shape soft drink demand and profitability across South Africa, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Ethiopia and Mozambique over the next 18 months: consumer affordability, currency, sugar taxes, packaging and recycling regulation, and modern vs informal retail. For each, give the evidence, the likely impact on a Coca-Cola bottler, and two moves leadership should consider. Use current, cited sources and finish with a one-page executive summary that clearly identifies:

- The decisions leadership should consider
- What CCBA should act on or test first
- The internal data needed to validate the recommendations
- What evidence could change the recommendations
- Five questions executives should ask before taking action
items.feature: Researcher agent.

items.title: Ideation sprint
items.prompt: I need to [DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF A TASK]. Search for relevant information both internally and externally. Summarise findings into a clear, digestible format. Provide five creative starting ideas to help me approach the task effectively and quickly.
items.feature: Work and web grounding with separate citations.
items.participant_tip: Replace the brackets with your task.

items.title: Strategic post-mortem
items.prompt: Act as a strategic reviewer helping me run a post-mortem on a project, launch, decision, or incident. Start by asking 3 clarifying questions one by one to gather the minimum necessary context before analysing anything. Do not produce the post-mortem until I’ve answered those questions. Ask focused questions that help define: the initiative or event under review, the original intent and expected outcomes, the timeline, scope, and stakeholders, what happened in practice, what evidence, metrics, or feedback exists, and any constraints, trade-offs, or major decisions already known. After that, produce a structured post-mortem with the following sections: What was expected; What actually happened; Where the biggest gaps appeared; Root causes; Decisions that helped; Decisions that hurt; Lessons learned; What we should repeat, stop, or change next time. Keep the analysis clear, objective, and practical. Focus on organisational learning, decision quality, and systemic improvement rather than blame. Call out uncertainty where evidence is incomplete, and separate observations, causes, and recommendations.
items.feature: Copilot asks clarifying questions one at a time before answering.

items.title: CEO template
items.prompt:
Act as my Executive Chief of Staff.
I am preparing to make or influence a strategic decision related to: [STRATEGIC INITIATIVE].
Use [INSERT DOCUMENT / BOARD DECK / MEETING / EMAIL THREAD] to create a CEO-level briefing.
Deliver exactly:
- What’s at stake (mission, financial sustainability, reputation)
- The 3 decisions I must make or shape
- Trade-offs across stakeholders (board, shareholders, staff, customers)
- Top 5 risks (including reputational and mission risk) + mitigations
- Second-order effects (what this triggers over 12–36 months)
- What I may be overestimating or underestimating
- 5 board-level talking points
- 5 high-impact questions I should ask
Close with:
- The single most important judgment call
- A 30-second CEO framing I can use with the board

items.title: CFO template
items.prompt:
Act as a CFO and financial steward.
Stress-test this initiative: [STRATEGIC INITIATIVE]
using [INSERT BUSINESS CASE / FINANCIAL MODEL].
Deliver:
- Where assumptions may be overly optimistic
- Full cost picture (hidden or downstream costs)
- Worst-case, base-case, and upside scenarios
- Cash flow and timing risks
- Financial trade-offs we are implicitly making
- Sensitivity analysis (what variables matter most)
Then:
- Identify 3 metrics I must track weekly
- Recommend a financial gating or checkpoint structure
Close with:
- The biggest financial risk I may be underestimating
- Whether this is reversible or a one-way commitment

items.title: COO template
items.prompt:
Act as my Chief Operating Officer advisor.
Evaluate how to operationalize this initiative: [STRATEGIC INITIATIVE]
using [INSERT PLAN / PROPOSAL / ROADMAP].
Deliver:
- What success actually looks like operationally (metrics, behaviors)
- Top execution dependencies (people, systems, partners)
- 5 operational risks (capacity, adoption, sequencing, etc.)
- Where this will break in real-world conditions
- Key decision points over the next 90 days
- What must NOT slip
Then:
- Build a 90-day execution plan with milestones
- Identify owners, risks, and success criteria for each
Close with:
- The single biggest execution risk
- What I should simplify or cut immediately

items.title: Chief People Officer (CHRO) template
items.prompt:
Act as my Chief People Officer.
Assess workforce and culture impact of:
[STRATEGIC INITIATIVE]
using [INSERT ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT].
Deliver:
- How different groups will react (leaders, frontline, managers)
- Top 5 adoption risks (skills, fear, trust, workload)

Then:

Close with:
